clue.text: Jack maybe set about it in the morning, turning all theatrical

indicators.note: turning everything round means the whole assembled string is read backwards
set about means placed around, so the card encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a jack is one kind of playing card
taken as written
AM is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack, rising early, suddenly makes a big show of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack maybe' suggests a sailor but is a playing card; 'set about' wraps it round the other pieces, and 'turning all' reads CITAMARD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is showy and stagy, a direct synonym of theatrical.

clue.text: End of stress — girl's going up the chart

parts.note: relief is the ending or easing of stress

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's stress ends as she rises up the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of stress' looks like the last letter S but is a whole word, RELIEF. 'going up' reverses PAM to MAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map is a chart that shows the height of the land.

clue.text: Performer in the Ring a little restricted by extra cut

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in by, so the next piece goes inside
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: more means extra, additional
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A singer in Wagner's opera cycle is somewhat limited by heavy trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Ring suggests Wagner's opera cycle, but the ring is the bullring. 'cut' docks a last letter to leave MOR, which 'restricted by' wraps round the little bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who performs the kill in the bullring.

clue.text: One needed to chew over what's stolen, including set of books

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
over means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone must chew over the thefts, including some accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the slang word for stolen into TOH, and 'including' sets the Bible's first books inside it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth is one of the things used for chewing food.

clue.text: Bird-watcher's pet hate?

parts.note: a pet that watches birds for prey, and the thing birders most detest

explanation.definitionFit: A domestic feline stalks birds, so it is both a watcher of birds and what birders loathe.

clue.text: Very nice translation perhaps lacking appeal

indicators.note: lacking means doing without, so letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a subtitle on a film is one kind of translation
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A rendering that is very pleasant but has no charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' here is its older sense of finely discriminating, which is why 'very nice' can define the answer. IT for sex appeal is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its precise sense means finely drawn, and a very fine distinction is a subtle one.

clue.text: Consistently block deliveries

parts.note: a cricket batsman who keeps defending against every ball bowled, never trying to score

explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall in cricket is to bat purely defensively; generally it means to obstruct steadily.

clue.text: Throw 'em out, of fancy bedroom -you and I phoned to be in it!

annotationWithheld.why: Scan reads 'Throw 'em out of fancy bedroom — you and I phoned to be in it!'; no parse of 'Throw 'em out' plus U and I gives BOUDOIR, and searches found no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Throw 'em out, of fancy bedroom -you and I phoned to be in it!

clue.text: Somewhat melodic ululation set up, very clear

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the run is backwards
somewhat means a part of, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: A tuneful wailing is raised, sounding crystal clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DICUL spans melodic and ululation; 'set up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means transparent or easily understood, so very clear.

clue.text: Concoct schemes in bed

definitions.meaning: a small piece of ground for growing plants, a garden bed

explanation.definitionFit: To plot is to scheme, and a plot is also a patch of ground such as a flower bed.

clue.text: Getting fed up in office hours, having gone crazy

definitions.text: Getting fed up in office hours
definitions.meaning: taking a meal break during the working day, away from the desk
slang for being mad or dotty

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a worker away eating, and idiomatically means mad.

clue.text: Why trouble besets close current play area

indicators.note: besets means surrounds, so the scrambled letters close around the next piece
to trouble is to stir up, so the letters of why are rearranged

parts.note: a close is an end or conclusion
the Ouse is an English river, and a river is a current

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a disturbance surrounds the end of a modern playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the first word into WYH, and 'besets' wraps that round the close after its first letter. The Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a small toy house children play in, a play area of sorts; the name comes from Peter Pan.

clue.text: Post deserving respect

definitions.meaning: honest and honourable, as in an upstanding citizen

explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical post, and an upright person is honest and respectable.

clue.text: Things not even given prices

definitions.meaning: odd numbers or items, those that are not even
betting prices, as offered by a bookmaker

explanation.definitionFit: Odd items are ones that are not even, and bookmakers' quoted prices are called odds.

clue.text: So it may appear a fraction unacceptable?

definitions.text: So it may appear a fraction
definitions.meaning: a fraction like seven-thirds, with a top larger than its bottom, carries this label

explanation.definitionFit: A top-heavy fraction is described with this word, which also means indecent or unacceptable.

clue.text: Try to clear the bar of sporty types getting very high

definitions.text: Try to clear the bar of sporty types getting very high

parts.words: Try to clear the bar of sporty types getting very high
parts.note: an athletic event in which competitors spring over a high crossbar using a long flexible pole

explanation.definitionFit: In this field event athletes vault very high to clear a raised bar.

clue.text: Sudden change in bar — put off?

indicators.note: a change in these letters means they are reordered
off here means out of order, a second sign to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub suddenly alters, leaving a customer discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change in' and 'off' both tell you to rearrange BAR and PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt event happens suddenly and without warning, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Finally trap elusive arboreal mammal

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the following word
elusive means slippery, hard to pin down, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: At last someone snares a shy tree-dwelling creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elusive' rearranges the tree-dwelling adjective into OLARBEAR. The surface's tree-dweller is a misdirection: the answer lives on Arctic ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is a large Arctic mammal.

clue.text: Maybe 13, inexperienced learner appears to be ungainly

parts.note: 13 across is ODDS, and SP is the starting price, one kind of odds in betting
raw means green, untrained
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Perhaps an awkward novice driver looks clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe 13' points to 13 across, ODDS; SP, the starting price, is a sort of odds. 'appears to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to spread one's limbs out awkwardly, so to look or be ungainly.

clue.text: Built-up area where workers congregate

parts.note: a mound piled up by insects, where the worker caste swarms, read like a description of a town

explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects build and crowd into this mound, which reads like an urban development.

clue.text: Chap accepts large bill sent over, in a naive way

clue.text: Playwright needing one individual's company

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
one's, the possessive of a single person, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dramatist needs a private company of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugène Ionesco was a French-Romanian absurdist playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionesco wrote plays such as Rhinoceros and The Bald Soprano.

clue.text: Not eating food quickly

definitions.meaning: to go without meals, as in a religious abstention

explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from meals, and the same word means rapidly.

clue.text: Head of school missed pointer to the way forward

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the school's name to be removed
missed means left out, so that first letter goes

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English boarding school

explanation.surface: A headteacher missed the sign showing which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is an English public school; drop its first letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign showing which direction to go.

clue.text: Change involves entire retraining of surgeons

indicators.note: involves means wraps up inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: to vary is to change

indicators.note: retraining reshapes the letters, so entire is rearranged

explanation.surface: A reform requires every doctor who operates to retrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retraining' rearranges the whole of the second word into ETERIN, which 'involves' sets inside the word for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterinary describes animal doctors, as in a veterinary surgeon, the British name for a vet.

clue.text: Grassed up? That'll sound a bit thin

definitions.meaning: covered with tall grassy plants, a playful reading of British slang for informing
describes a voice or tone that is high and weak

explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means full of reeds, which are grasses, and also describes a thin piping tone.

clue.text: Clearly stating view of joints

definitions.meaning: in biology the word describes something made of jointed segments, so it gives that view of a jointed body

explanation.definitionFit: An articulate speaker expresses things clearly, and an articulate limb is one that is jointed.

clue.text: Request time off work

indicators.note: off means taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone requests leave from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time off' reads like leave but means remove T from TASK.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to request something.

clue.text: Check section of pipe

definitions.meaning: to halt or stop a flow
the thin tube of a tobacco pipe running to the mouthpiece

explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to check it, and the shaft of a tobacco pipe has the same name.

clue.text: Somewhat dim idiot I left on board

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, as aboard a ship, so letters go inside

parts.note: a twit is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A half-witted fool says he left something on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat dim' tempts as part of describing the idiot, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit only faintly by twilight, so partly dark or dim.

clue.text: Vital poet retains old facility for writing

parts.note: key means essential, vital

indicators.note: retains means keeps inside, so the poet holds the next letter

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An important writer of verse keeps an antiquated aid for composing.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard is the device used for typing, so a facility for writing.
